It's great that you're taking steps to get your novel ready for submission! That said, this opening may not be the most compelling way to hook an agent. Starting with "It was a dark and stormy night" is a well-known cliché, which might make it harder for your work to stand out. Additionally, using "sad, very very sad" comes across as repetitive and tells the reader how Sarah feels instead of showing it through her actions, environment, or inner thoughts.

Consider starting with a vivid or intriguing moment, an unusual detail, or an emotional cue that draws readers into Sarah’s world and makes them curious about her story. A strong, original first line will set the tone and grab attention. Keep working at it — you've got this!

I'm sorry your week has been so challenging—it sounds like you've had to juggle a lot. It’s frustrating when small things, like burned rice, feel like the tipping point. Be kind to yourself; it’s okay to feel overwhelmed sometimes.

As for Mr. Okonkwo, if he's been reasonable in the past, it sounds like you can approach him with honesty and respect. Here's an example of what you could say to explain your situation:

Subject: Rent Payment Update

Dear Mr. Okonkwo,

I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to reach out to let you know that unfortunately, I will need to make my rent payment a bit later than usual this month. I apologize for any inconvenience this may cause and want to assure you that I’m working on resolving the delay as quickly as possible. I expect to be able to make the payment by [specific date].

Thank you so much for your understanding and patience. Please let me know if there’s anything else I should provide or do in the meantime.

Best regards,
[Your Name]

This type of wording acknowledges the situation, apologizes, and provides a clear time frame, while also showing consideration for his position as the landlord. Hopefully this helps lighten a little of the load for you. Hang in there—you’ve got this.

s20.html:
Honesty is definitely a strength in relationships—being open and truthful helps build trust and authenticity. However, there's also a balance to strike in how honesty is expressed. Sometimes, it’s not just about being honest; it’s about how honesty is communicated. There’s a difference between being honest in a constructive, compassionate way versus being blunt in a way that might hurt someone or come across as overly critical.

It’s worth reflecting on what "too honest" might have looked like in your past relationships. Were there instances where your honesty might have lacked sensitivity or timing? It’s also possible your ex-partners had difficulty receiving feedback or managing conflict, but considering both sides can give you insight into patterns and how you might approach future relationships.

If you're prioritizing honesty but doing so with empathy and respect, that is absolutely a strength and a key ingredient for a healthy relationship. Communicating in a way that fosters understanding, rather than defensiveness, will likely lead to more positive experiences in your future connections.
